brief: State the design as numbers before you draw a single box. Eight numbers are enough to tell you whether an agent design can work at all.
Change any number and the operating envelope recomputes: peak concurrency by Little's law, cost per task, p95 latency, and end-to-end success compounded across every step.
Challenge: the research-assistant preset breaks two checks. Requirement numbers are locked. Change only the design numbers until all four checks pass.

fields.label: Tasks per day
fields.help: Daily volume the system must absorb.

fields.label: Peak-to-average ratio
fields.help: How much busier the busiest minute is than the daily average.

fields.label: p95 latency target
fields.help: 95 per cent of tasks must finish within this time.

fields.label: Cost ceiling per task
fields.help: The most one task may spend on model tokens.

fields.label: Steps per task
fields.help: Average model calls in the loop for one task.

fields.label: Tokens per step
fields.help: Input plus output tokens per model call.

fields.label: Seconds per step
fields.help: Average wall time of one step, model plus tools.

fields.label: Per-step success rate
fields.help: Probability one step is correct. Raising it means adding verification or retries.

presets.title: Support triage agent
presets.story: Classify and route 40,000 support tickets a day, answering simple ones directly.

presets.title: Research assistant
presets.story: Read internal documents and write a cited two-page brief. Long horizon, many steps.

presets.title: Invoice matcher
presets.story: Match supplier invoices to purchase orders overnight in a batch.

challenge.instruction: Make all four checks pass without touching the requirement numbers. Hint: success compounds per step, so the step count is the strongest lever.
